messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: bug in multiply_log()
parts:
Hi all,

I think I've tracked down the bug that was causing adaptation to hang in rats (and dyes? and other things?). Well, almost tracked down.

The basic issue is that the value we're computing for the gradient of the multiply_double() function is off by 2. Why this is is a bit of a mystery to me. But if you replace the multiply_log(alpha+1.0, y) call in inv_gamma_log() with (alpha+1.0)*log(y), then everything works fine.

Also: what's the deal with the different versions of multiply_log() in the stan/agrad/special_functions.hpp and stan/maths/special_functions.hpp? The first one does not seem to be getting called when gradients are computed.

Finally: can I re-check in my testGradients() function in prob_grad.hpp? It's really really useful for finding bugs like this, and it's useful if you want to code your own gradients for speed.

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bug in multiply_log()
parts:
Nice sleuthing. I'll take care of the multiply_log
situation. That got added to deal with the 0 log 0 case.

Templated special functions without any reference to
agrad are going in stan::maths (and in stan/maths) and
the refs to agrad are going in stan/agrad. Now I think
we probably want to drop everything back into the
stan::maths namespace, otherwise we won't be able to
use explicit calls and will have to do multiple "using"
statements (which is actually the preferred way of
doing things in some contexts).

Feel free to drop testGradients() back in prob_grad.hpp.

We can figure out where it goes later.

I think basic finite diffs functionality should be
in stan::maths. Then the test for prob_grad can
go elsewhere. The general thing to do is to take
general functor arguments and wrap up prob_grad
as a functor. That'd make it the right sort of thing
to drop into an optimizer, too. I'll figure out
how to do this the right way over the weekend.

- Bob
